Why does this streaming worker keep growing memory even though every promise resolves?

The producer is scheduling work faster than the consumer can drain it. Resolved promises do not bound the queued closures or their captured buffers. Put a fixed-capacity semaphore before scheduling, await capacity release after each consumer finishes, and stop admitting new work when cancellation begins. This makes memory proportional to the concurrency limit rather than the input length.
We checked keys and TTLs. Why did only requests in one region miss?

The decisive observation is that the affected region used a different deployment revision whose cache namespace still included the old schema version. The fix is to derive the namespace once from the deployed schema identifier and pass it to both readers and writers. Add a startup assertion that logs the resolved namespace so a regional mismatch is visible before traffic arrives.
Can we turn the lessons from this migration into a reusable decision framework?

Use a four-part reversible automation test: identify the authoritative state, preview the exact mutation, bind the live mutation to the previewed version, and persist a receipt immediately after success. If any precondition changes, defer instead of reconstructing intent. Recovery should prove an existing receipt or marker rather than repeating the original decision. This separates semantic planning from deterministic mutation safety.

Summarize the retry budget rule and save it.

A retry budget caps retries as a fraction of successful traffic, preventing a failing dependency from multiplying load. The budget is consumed before a retry and replenished by successful primary requests.

parts.text: Explain the state transitions, then append today's purchase to my shopping note.

A circuit breaker moves from closed to open after the failure threshold, then to half-open after a cooldown. Half-open admits a bounded probe; success closes the breaker and failure reopens it. Keep the transition clock monotonic so wall-clock adjustments cannot prematurely admit probes.

parts.text: What is the practical checkpoint behavior of SQLite WAL mode?

WAL readers can continue while a writer appends frames, but checkpoints may be unable to reset the log while an older reader still holds its snapshot. Operationally, track long-lived readers when WAL size grows unexpectedly. Source: https://example.test/sqlite/wal

Separate the durable API and worker decisions into their linked notes.
For the API, use cursor pagination with a stable tie-breaker so inserts cannot cause duplicates between pages. The cursor must encode both the sort timestamp and immutable row ID.

For the worker, acknowledge only after the idempotency receipt commits. A crash before the receipt leaves the message visible for retry; a crash after it is safe because the handler proves the receipt before repeating work.
Explain why preview-first rollout is useful in the linked settings note.

Preview-first rollout exposes exact intended changes while preserving the current authoritative state. Operators can inspect routing and rendered content, adjust settings, and only then enable live mutation. The linked destination is machinery-owned settings content and must not receive synthesized capture text.
Pull out the reusable ideas from both topics.

For cache invalidation, name every cache entry by the authoritative version of the data it represents. Publishing a new version makes old entries unreachable without an eager delete pass, and rollback simply restores the previous version pointer.

For civil-time schedules, recompute the next local wall-clock occurrence in the target timezone after each run. Adding twenty-four hours to the previous instant drifts across daylight-saving transitions and can duplicate or skip intended local times.
We disproved the linked note's retry assumption. What should be retained?

Retain the contradiction explicitly instead of rewriting history: the prior note assumes every timeout is safe to retry, but the payment endpoint can commit before its response is lost. Future retries require an idempotency key and durable result lookup. Append the correction with the evidence date so readers can distinguish the old assumption from the new conclusion.
